summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style biography of Javier Barros Sierra (1915-1971), a Mexican civil engineer and Rector of UNAM. It covers his birth in Mexico City, his studies and teaching career at UNAM, and his tenure as Rector from May 5, 1966. It focuses on his resignation on September 23, 1968, in protest at the government and army entering Ciudad Universitaria, nine days before the Tlatelolco massacre, and his reinstatement after CU was liberated, until May 5, 1970.
one_line: Biography of Javier Barros Sierra, Mexican engineer and UNAM Rector who resigned in protest before the 1968 Tlatelolco massacre.
key_facts: Javier Barros Sierra lived from 1915 to 1971 and was a Mexican engineer.
Javier Barros Sierra was Rector of the National Autonomous University of Mexico during the 1968 Tlatelolco massacre.
Javier Barros Sierra was born in Mexico City and studied civil engineering at UNAM.
Javier Barros Sierra became president of the student society of the Faculty of Sciences in 1936.
Javier Barros Sierra became University Counsellor in 1938.
Javier Barros Sierra taught for more than 20 years at the Escuela Nacional Preparatoria and the National School of Engineering.
Javier Barros Sierra was director of the National School of Engineering from 1955 to 1958.
Javier Barros Sierra became Rector of UNAM on May 5, 1966.
During Javier Barros Sierra's rectorship, the government and the army entered Ciudad Universitaria, UNAM's main campus.
Javier Barros Sierra resigned as Rector on September 23, in protest of the entry of the government and army into Ciudad Universitaria and the indiscriminate beating of UNAM's students.
Javier Barros Sierra's resignation came 9 days before the massacre in Tlatelolco.
Javier Barros Sierra was reinstated as Rector after the liberation of Ciudad Universitaria.
Javier Barros Sierra held the post of Rector until May 5, 1970.
